label: Formulated concordant and complementary countertransference as the core diagnostic instrument
description: Racker established that the analyst's emotional countertransference is an indispensable instrument for diagnosing the patient's split internal object world.
historicalContext: Published in 'Transference and Countertransference' (1968), based on clinical papers presented in Buenos Aires in 1953-1957.
dialecticalTension: Transforming countertransference from an analyst's neurotic blindspot into an objective epistemological compass.

citations.author: Heinrich Racker
citations.sectionOrPage: Chapter 4: The Meanings and Uses of Countertransference

label: Radically inverted Freud's warning against countertransference into the primary therapeutic guide
description: Freud viewed countertransference as a blind spot to be overcome; Racker proved it to be the royal road to the patient's unconscious object relations.
historicalContext: Racker critiqued Freud's 1910 paper 'The Future Prospects of Psycho-Analytic Therapy' to establish modern countertransference utilization.
dialecticalTension: From classical surgical impassivity (the analyst as blank mirror) to interactive emotional resonance.

label: Racker's countertransference taxonomy formed the clinical core of Transference-Focused Psychotherapy
description: Otto Kernberg made Racker's concordant and complementary countertransference analysis the centerpiece of treating borderline personality organization.
historicalContext: Kernberg credited Racker in 'Borderline Conditions and Pathological Narcissism' (1975) and clinical manuals.
dialecticalTension: Using the therapist's complementary countertransference dread and rage to diagnose primitive projective identification.
